Vendored static libraries for heif-sys
=======================================

This directory holds prebuilt static libraries + public headers for the HEIF/AVIF decode
stack, so `cargo build` works with no native package manager or build tooling (no vcpkg /
cmake / meson / nasm) on the developer's machine. Only the linked-in machine code reaches
the shipped binary; the rest is dead-stripped by the linker at release time.

Layout: one directory per vendored target
-----------------------------------------
  x64-windows/     MSVC x64 static libs  (triplet x64-windows-static-md)
  arm64-macos/     Apple Silicon static libs (triplet arm64-osx)

Each holds BOTH `include/` and `lib/` from the same vcpkg run. The headers are per-target,
not shared: the two targets are not necessarily at the same upstream libheif version, and
bindgen must parse the headers that match the libs it will link. build.rs picks a directory
from CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS/ARCH and fails with a named error on any other target.

Contents
--------
  x64-windows/lib/heif.lib        libheif  1.23.0  (HEIF/AVIF container + API, C++) [LGPL-3.0-only]
  x64-windows/lib/libde265.lib    libde265 1.1.1   (HEVC decoder, for HEIC/HEIF, C++)[LGPL-3.0-only]
  x64-windows/lib/dav1d.lib       dav1d            (AV1 decoder, for AVIF, C)        [BSD-2-Clause]
  arm64-macos/lib/libheif.a       libheif  1.23.2  (same, arm64)                     [LGPL-3.0-only]
  arm64-macos/lib/libde265.a      libde265         (same, arm64)                     [LGPL-3.0-only]
  arm64-macos/lib/libdav1d.a      dav1d            (same, arm64)                     [BSD-2-Clause]
  <target>/include/libheif/*      libheif public C headers for that target

Version drift: Windows is at libheif 1.23.0 and macOS at 1.23.2, because they were vendored
from different vcpkg baselines. The differences are additive (new HDR-metadata APIs, mostly in
the unused C++ header) and none touch the C API `wrapper.c` calls, but converge them on the
next re-vendor of either side.

How these were produced (one-time, on a machine with vcpkg)
----------------------------------------------------------
The stock vcpkg libheif port offers AVIF only via aom (large, slower decode) and pulls the
x265 ENCODER via its default `hevc` feature. We want AVIF via dav1d (small, fast) and no
encoders, so patch the local port before installing:

  1. ports/libheif/vcpkg.json    : add "dav1d" to the top-level "dependencies" array.
  2. ports/libheif/portfile.cmake: change  -DWITH_DAV1D=OFF  ->  -DWITH_DAV1D=ON
  3. ports/libheif/portfile.cmake: add     -DENABLE_PLUGIN_LOADING=OFF
     REQUIRED ON macOS, harmless on Windows. libheif's CMake defaults ENABLE_PLUGIN_LOADING
     to ON, and where the platform supports it dav1d is then built as a *separate dynamic
     plugin* (plugins/libheif/libheif-dav1d.so) instead of being compiled into libheif. In a
     static build that plugin is unreachable, and the failure is silent: libheif.a links fine
     and carries no dav1d references at all, so every AVIF simply fails to decode at runtime.
     Verify after building:  nm -u lib/libheif.a | grep -c dav1d   (must be > 0)
  4. Build (the [core] feature set drops the default x265 encoder):
       Windows:  vcpkg install "libheif[core]:x64-windows-static-md"
       macOS:    vcpkg install "libheif[core]:arm64-osx"
     vcpkg auto-acquires the nasm/meson/ninja that dav1d needs.

Then copy `installed/<triplet>/include/libheif` and the three libs from
`installed/<triplet>/lib` into this directory's target subdirectory.

Stripping (Windows only — why those libs are ~52 MB, not ~220 MB)
------------------------------------------------------------------
vcpkg's release build on MSVC embeds CodeView debug info (/Z7) directly in the .obj files,
which balloons heif.lib to ~194 MB. The debug info is useless in a vendored lib (and Rust
strips it from release binaries anyway), so it is removed with llvm-objcopy:

       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug heif.lib     heif.lib
       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug dav1d.lib    dav1d.lib
       llvm-objcopy --strip-debug libde265.lib libde265.lib

This only drops .debug$S/.debug$T sections; code, symbols, and the /DEFAULTLIB directives
(which auto-link the MSVC C++ runtime for libheif/libde265) are preserved. The arm64-osx
release build carries no such debug info — those .a files are ~6 MB as produced.

Linking
-------
Windows: the MSVC objects embed /DEFAULTLIB directives for the C++ runtime libheif and
libde265 need, so it links itself and build.rs must not name it.
macOS: Mach-O has no equivalent, so build.rs names `c++` explicitly or libheif's and
libde265's C++ symbols go unresolved.

Updating
--------
Re-run the recipe above against a newer vcpkg, re-strip (Windows), and replace the files in
that target's subdirectory. Keep the triplets at x64-windows-static-md / arm64-osx.
